articles.title: India-ASEAN Maritime Cooperation Framework: Strengthening Indo-Pacific Security Architecture
articles.summary: India and ASEAN countries advance a collaborative maritime security framework focusing on freedom of navigation and supply chain resilience.
prelims: ASEAN was established in 1967 via the Bangkok Declaration.
India became a Sectoral Dialogue Partner of ASEAN in 1992 and Full Dialogue Partner in 1996.
UNCLOS (1982) defines the legal status of Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) extending up to 200 nautical miles from baselines.
articles.mains: Analyze the geopolitical significance of ASEAN centrality in India's Act East Policy and its strategic implications for maritime security in the Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: National Bio-Foundry Network: Accelerating Synthetic Biology under the BioE3 Policy
articles.summary: The Ministry of Science and Technology operationalizes advanced bio-foundries to foster high-tech biomanufacturing and industrial decarbonization.
prelims: Bio-foundries integrate synthetic biology, automation, and artificial intelligence to design and test biological systems.
The BioE3 Policy stands for Economy, Environment, and Employment.
Key focus sectors include bioplastics, precision therapeutics, and enzyme-based industrial synthesis.
articles.mains: Examine how synthetic biology and biomanufacturing can transform India's industrial landscape while aiding its net-zero emissions commitment.

articles.title: Critical Minerals Security: KABIL Secures Overseas Exploration Blocks for Lithium and Cobalt
articles.summary: Khanij Bidesh India Limited expands its overseas footprints in South America to safeguard India's green energy supply chain.
prelims: KABIL is a joint venture of NALCO, HCL, and MECL under the Ministry of Mines.
The 'Lithium Triangle' consists of Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile.
Critical minerals like Lithium, Cobalt, and Rare Earth Elements (REEs) are crucial for EV batteries and renewable storage systems.
articles.mains: Discuss India's strategy to achieve critical mineral security and evaluate its role in mitigating global supply chain vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Digital Public Infrastructure in Rural Governance: CAG Report Evaluates Last-Mile Impact
articles.summary: A CAG audit assesses the effectiveness, transparency, and data privacy compliance of India Stack implementations across Panchayati Raj institutions.
prelims: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is a constitutional authority established under Article 148 of the Indian Constitution.
India Stack consists of three distinct layers: Identity (Aadhaar), Payments (UPI), and Data Sharing (Account Aggregator framework).
The Digital Agriculture Mission incorporates the AgriStack platform for unified farmer identification.
articles.mains: Evaluate the impact of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) on enhancing transparency and reducing corruption in rural service delivery.

articles.title: RBI Expands Offline and Cross-Border Functionality of Central Bank Digital Currency (e-₹)
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India introduces offline transaction protocols and cross-border payment integration for the Digital Rupee.
prelims: CBDC is a sovereign currency issued by a central bank in digital form, holding legal tender status equal to physical cash.
Retail CBDC (e-₹-R) is designed for public use, whereas Wholesale CBDC (e-₹-W) is meant for interbank settlements.
Offline CBDC implementations rely on Near Field Communication (NFC) and hardware-based secure elements.
articles.mains: Assess the potential of Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) to reduce cash logistics costs and streamline international remittances.
